title: 3-SAT and clique equivalence
statement: Let $V$ be any type and let $f$ be a list of $m$ clauses, each consisting of three literals over $V$. The formula $f$ is satisfiable if and only if its conflict graph has a clique of size $m$. The graph's vertices are clause-position pairs, and two are adjacent exactly when they come from different clauses and their literals are not opposite occurrences of the same variable.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a finite list of three-literal clauses over $V$
replaced:
Let $f$ be a 3-CNF formula with $m$ clauses. Then $f$ is satisfiable if and only if its
conflict graph has a clique of size $m$; that is, the graph whose vertices are the
literal positions of $f$, with two positions adjacent exactly when they lie in different
clauses and their literals do not conflict, contains $m$ pairwise-adjacent vertices
precisely when some truth assignment satisfies every clause of $f$.
